objective: Add a new module `demo_app/slug.py` with a function `slugify(text: str) -> str` that turns text into a URL-safe slug. The ASCII alphanumeric characters are exactly `a-z`, `A-Z` and `0-9`; every other character (spaces, punctuation, underscores, and all non-ASCII characters such as `é`) is non-alphanumeric. Rules: (1) ASCII letters are lower-cased; digits are kept; (2) every maximal run of one or more non-alphanumeric characters is replaced by a single `-`; (3) leading and trailing `-` are removed; (4) if the result is empty, return the string `n-a`.
acceptance: slugify('Hello World') returns 'hello-world' and slugify('already-a-slug') returns 'already-a-slug'
A run of separators becomes one dash: slugify('a   b') returns 'a-b', slugify('a - b') returns 'a-b' and slugify('a__b!!c') returns 'a-b-c'
Leading and trailing separators are removed: slugify('  Hello, World!  ') returns 'hello-world' and slugify('---x---') returns 'x'
Digits are kept: slugify('Release 3.0 RC-2') returns 'release-3-0-rc-2'
Non-ASCII characters count as separators: slugify('Café Au Lait') returns 'caf-au-lait'
If nothing alphanumeric remains, the result is 'n-a': slugify('') , slugify('   '), slugify('!!!') and slugify('é') all return 'n-a'
The result never starts or ends with '-' (except that 'n-a' contains a dash inside) and never contains '--'
